evidence.quote: Mary , it was wrong of you to be so late

claims.adjudication_reason: A directly addresses B as 'Mary' in turns 1 and 7, explicitly establishing B's name.

evidence.quote: it was wrong of you to be so late

claims.adjudication_reason: A's statement 'it was wrong of you to be so late' presupposes B's lateness as an established fact.

claims.claim: B has a mother who is very worried
claims.adjudication_reason: 'Mother's very worried' with definite 'Mother' presupposes a mother exists and is worried. Whether this is B's own mother or a shared mother, the worry is directed at B's lateness, making it reasonable to attribute a worried mother to B.

claims.claim: B shares a mother with A (they are siblings)
claims.attribute: B and A have the same mother
claims.adjudication_reason: Second-review support: The bare definite kinship term 'Mother' (capitalized, no possessive) is a conventional presupposition in English that the referent is shared between speaker and listener. If A meant only their own mother, 'my mother' would be used; if only Mary's mother, 'your mother' would be used. The unmodified 'Mother' presupposes a shared parent, establishing the sibling relationship.
